# Drshya Design System

Drshya is Yantra's own design system. It ships as the `@yantra/ui` workspace package in
`packages/ui`, and every screen of the coming Yantra app is meant to be built from it. It
provides color, glass, type, shape and motion tokens on Tailwind CSS v4, one semantic icon
registry, and 16 accessible primitive families on React Aria Components.

Its value is that later app features cannot drift from the design language, from accessibility, or
from the security rules, because the build, lint and a real-Chrome harness enforce them. A token
pairing that misses WCAG contrast fails the build. A raw palette class or a direct `lucide-react`
import fails lint. A primitive without a gallery entry fails a unit test. A CSP violation, a request
to another origin, an axe-core violation or a missing focus ring fails the harness.

This is a maintainer and integrator feature. Nothing in it is visible to Yantra users yet: no app
mounts it, and it adds no CLI command. Package internals, the token pipeline diagram and the build
order are in [Architecture: `packages/ui` (Drshya)](../architecture.md#packagesui-drshya) and
[Architecture: Drshya gallery harness](../architecture.md#drshya-gallery-harness).

## What It Does

### Keeps every color in one TypeScript source, in three tiers

Every color value lives once in `packages/ui/src/tokens/` as OKLCH. `scripts/emit-tokens.ts`
generates `src/styles/theme.generated.css` from that data, so the CSS and the contrast checks always
use the same numbers. The generated file is listed in `.prettierignore` and must never be edited by
hand.

| Tier      | Where it lives                                | How it reaches CSS                                                                            | Who uses it                     |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Primitive | `palette.ts`: 13 fog steps, Ion, four signals | Plain custom properties on `:root` (`--drshya-fog-05`, `--drshya-ion-fill`), never utilities  | Only the semantic map           |
| Semantic  | `semantic.ts`: `SEMANTIC_COLORS`              | Tailwind `@theme` (`--color-surface`), which generates utilities (`bg-surface`, `text-ink-2`) | Components                      |
| Component | `drshya.css` and the generated `:root` block  | Plain properties (`--glass-alpha`, `--dialog-scrim`)                                          | Single components and utilities |

The fog ramp is 13 cool neutrals at hue 255 that are the same in both themes:

| Step   | OKLCH             | Step   | OKLCH             |
| ------ | ----------------- | ------ | ----------------- |
| fog-00 | `0.994 0.002 255` | fog-60 | `0.53 0.011 255`  |
| fog-05 | `0.975 0.004 255` | fog-70 | `0.42 0.011 255`  |
| fog-10 | `0.952 0.005 255` | fog-80 | `0.31 0.01 255`   |
| fog-20 | `0.915 0.006 255` | fog-90 | `0.22 0.009 255`  |
| fog-30 | `0.862 0.007 255` | fog-95 | `0.165 0.008 255` |
| fog-40 | `0.76 0.009 255`  | fog-99 | `0.125 0.007 255` |
| fog-50 | `0.64 0.01 255`   |        |                   |

The semantic tier is a closed list of 23 names. Each maps to one primitive per theme:

| Semantic token         | Light                     | Dark                    | Meaning                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `bg`                   | fog-05                    | fog-99                  | Page background                                       |
| `surface`              | fog-00                    | fog-95                  | Paper that content sits on                            |
| `sunken`               | fog-10                    | fog-99                  | Inputs, table headers, hover fills                    |
| `ink`                  | fog-95                    | fog-05                  | Primary text                                          |
| `ink-2`                | fog-70                    | fog-40                  | Secondary text, the agent voice                       |
| `ink-3`                | fog-60                    | fog-50                  | Tertiary and disabled text (solid surfaces only)      |
| `rule`, `rule-strong`  | fog-20, fog-30            | fog-90, fog-80          | Dividers and stronger borders                         |
| `field-edge`           | fog-60                    | fog-50                  | The 3:1 boundary of a form control                    |
| `accent`               | Ion fill `0.54 0.097 218` | Ion fill `0.8 0.14 218` | Primary fills and the focus ring                      |
| `on-accent`            | `1 0 0` (white)           | `0.18 0.03 230`         | Text on `accent`                                      |
| `accent-ink`           | `0.5 0.089 218`           | `0.82 0.12 218`         | Link and accent text; the primary button's hover fill |
| `signal-fulfilled`     | Jade `0.55 0.12 162`      | `0.76 0.14 162`         | Graphic: glyphs, fills and rings                      |
| `signal-partial`       | Amber `0.62 0.139 65`     | `0.8 0.14 65`           | Graphic                                               |
| `signal-failed`        | Crimson `0.55 0.2 25`     | `0.7 0.18 25`           | Graphic                                               |
| `signal-needs-you`     | Rani `0.55 0.22 352`      | `0.72 0.2 352`          | Graphic                                               |
| `signal-fulfilled-ink` | `0.51 0.111 162`          | same as the graphic     | Text in the signal's hue                              |
| `signal-partial-ink`   | `0.54 0.121 65`           | same as the graphic     | Text                                                  |
| `signal-failed-ink`    | same as the graphic       | same as the graphic     | Text                                                  |
| `signal-needs-you-ink` | same as the graphic       | same as the graphic     | Text                                                  |
| `glass-tint`           | fog-00                    | fog-95                  | The glass color, drawn at `--glass-alpha`             |
| `glass-edge`           | fog-20                    | fog-80                  | The glass border                                      |
| `glass-spec`           | fog-00                    | fog-40                  | The glass top highlight                               |

Each signal has two tokens. The graphic token must reach 3:1 as a non-text element, and the `-ink`
token must reach 4.5:1 as text. In the light theme, Jade and Amber need a darker ink than their
graphic, so the two differ. Aborted has no signal color: it uses `ink-2` with the
`outcome.aborted` ban icon.

Some light values differ from the brainstorm on purpose. The light Ion fill is lightness 0.54, not
0.55, so white text reaches 4.5:1. Light Ion, Jade and Amber also keep their lightness and hue but
use the largest chroma that is inside the sRGB gamut. Without that, a wide-gamut display would show a
color the contrast gate never measured.

### Follows the OS theme or an explicit one

Light and dark are chosen by attributes, and nothing in Drshya stores a preference:

- With no `data-theme` attribute, the theme follows the OS (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- `data-theme="dark"` or `data-theme="light"` on any element pins that theme for the element and
  its subtree, even when the OS asks for the other one.
- Each theme block also sets `color-scheme`, so native controls and scrollbars follow it.

`applyAppearance(element, { theme, surfaces })` sets the attributes. `theme` is `'system'`,
`'light'` or `'dark'`, and `'system'` removes `data-theme`. `surfaces` is `'glass'` or `'solid'` and
sets `data-surfaces`. `appearanceAttributes()` returns the same attributes as an object you can
spread onto a JSX element. `parseAppearance(theme, surfaces)` reads untrusted strings, such as a
query string, and falls back to `{ theme: 'system', surfaces: 'glass' }` for anything it does not
recognize.

The stylesheet also defines two Tailwind variants. `dark:` follows the resolved theme, including
the OS case. `solid:` applies under Solid mode.

### Fails the build on any contrast, gamut or glass problem

The token generator checks the data before it writes any CSS. If anything breaks the contract, it
throws one `TokenContractError` that lists every problem, not just the first one:

- **Gamut**: a primitive is outside the sRGB gamut in a theme.
- **Reference**: a semantic token points at a primitive that does not exist.
- **Contrast**: a declared pairing misses its minimum in a theme. Text needs 4.5:1. Non-text
  elements (glyphs, fills, rings and boundaries) need 3:1.
- **Glass floor**: a token allowed as glass text would need a tint above the 0.85 cap. See the
  next section.

Each failure prints on one line, such as `on-accent/accent (light) 4.39 < 4.5`. A failing ratio is
never rounded up to a value that looks like a pass. A contrast failure on an out-of-gamut token is
measured on the clipped color, so the gamut and contrast failures appear in the same error.

The declared pairings (`CONTRAST_PAIRINGS`) are checked in both themes:

| Foreground                                                               | Background                      | Kind     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- | -------- |
| `ink`, `ink-2`, `ink-3`, `accent-ink` and the four `signal-*-ink` tokens | `bg`, `surface`, `sunken`       | text     |
| `on-accent`                                                              | `accent`, `accent-ink`          | text     |
| `surface` (tooltip text)                                                 | `ink`                           | text     |
| The four graphic `signal-*` tokens and `field-edge`                      | `bg`, `surface`, `sunken`       | non-text |
| `accent` (the focus ring)                                                | `bg`, `surface`                 | non-text |
| `ink`, `ink-2`                                                           | glass over black and over white | text     |

The gate runs in three places:

- The package `build` script runs `tsx scripts/emit-tokens.ts --check` first. `--check` writes
  nothing. It exits 1 when the contract fails, or when the checked-in CSS is missing or differs from
  a fresh emit.
- `tests/tokens/contrast-gate.spec.ts` asserts every pairing and the deliberate deviations.
- `tests/tokens/generated-drift.spec.ts` compares the checked-in CSS with a fresh emit byte for
  byte, after normalizing line endings.

### Makes glass legible by construction

The `glass` utility draws a translucent panel:

- a background of `glass-tint` at `--glass-alpha`;
- `backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(1.5)`;
- a 1 px `glass-edge` border, an inset 1 px top highlight in `glass-spec`, and the `shadow-glass`
  shadow;
- a repeating noise tile (`src/styles/assets/glass-noise.png`) at `--glass-noise-alpha` (0.03), to
  prevent banding.

The tint opacity is computed, not chosen. Glass can sit over any backdrop, and in the sRGB cube pure
black and pure white are the two extremes for contrast. The generator composites the tint over both
(source-over in gamma-encoded sRGB, as Chrome does) and shifts each result toward black and toward
white by the noise opacity. The **scrim floor** is the smallest opacity, in 0.005 steps rounded up,
at which every glass text token reaches 4.5:1 on all of those composites. The shipped
`--glass-alpha` is the larger of the brainstorm recipe (0.66 light, 0.72 dark) and that floor.

| Token        | Floor (light) | Floor (dark) | Allowed as text on glass? |
| ------------ | ------------- | ------------ | ------------------------- |
| `ink`        | 0.5           | 0.61         | Yes                       |
| `ink-2`      | 0.775         | 0.8          | Yes, and it sets the tint |
| `accent-ink` | 0.925         | 0.735        | No: light exceeds 0.85    |
| `ink-3`      | 0.97          | 0.93         | No                        |

The shipped values are `--glass-alpha: 0.775` in light and `0.8` in dark. Only `ink` and `ink-2`
(`GLASS_TEXT_TOKENS`) may be text on glass. A token joins that list only if its floor stays at or
below 0.85 in both themes, and the generator refuses the build otherwise. On glass, Ion appears
only as a graphic: the focus ring, icons and the selected-option check mark. Signal colors on glass
follow the same rule. Toasts and destructive menu items put the signal in an icon and keep their text
in `ink` or `ink-2`.

### Swaps glass for opaque Solid surfaces

Solid mode replaces every `glass` surface with the opaque `surface` color, a `rule-strong` border,
no backdrop filter, no noise and no shadow. Either trigger turns it on:

- `data-surfaces="solid"` on the element or an ancestor (`applyAppearance` with
  `surfaces: 'solid'`);
- the OS asking for reduced transparency (`prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce`), even when no
  attribute is set.

Components can use the `solid:` variant to adjust details under either trigger.

### Sets type, space, radius and motion as tokens

Fonts are self-hosted from the pinned Fontsource packages, so the app makes no font request to
another origin. The stylesheet imports Archivo with its width axis (normal and italic) and Martian
Mono with its width axis. `font-sans` is `"Archivo Variable", system-ui, sans-serif`, and
`font-mono` is `"Martian Mono Variable", ui-monospace, monospace`.

The three voices, plus a label and display style, are utilities:

| Utility        | Voice or use                | Style                                                                    |
| -------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `type-body`    | The person, plain text      | Sans, 100% width, weight 400                                             |
| `type-agent`   | The agent                   | Sans italic, `ink-2` color                                               |
| `type-engine`  | The engine: IDs, URLs, refs | Mono at 87.5% width, tabular numbers                                     |
| `type-label`   | Labels and tab lists        | Sans at 125% width, weight 650, uppercase, 0.08em tracking, `micro` size |
| `type-display` | Large figures               | Sans at 112.5% width, weight 650, `display` size, tabular numbers        |

| Text size  | Size                                 | Line height |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------- |
| `micro`    | 0.72rem                              | 1.4         |
| `caption`  | 0.8125rem                            | 1.4         |
| `body`     | 0.9375rem                            | 1.5         |
| `lead`     | 1.125rem                             | 1.5         |
| `title`    | 1.5rem                               | 1.25        |
| `headline` | 2.25rem                              | 1.15        |
| `display`  | `clamp(2.25rem, 1rem + 4vw, 4.1rem)` | 1.05        |

Shape and motion:

- **Radius**: `rounded-chip` (4px, chips and badges), `rounded-control` (8px, controls),
  `rounded-frame` (14px, frames and dialogs) and `rounded-full`. No other radius exists.
- **Shadow**: `shadow-glass` is the only shadow.
- **Space**: spacing keeps Tailwind's `--spacing` of 0.25rem (the 4 px base). There is no compact
  density.
- **Motion**: `--duration-quick` (120ms), `--duration-base` (200ms) and `--duration-slow` (320ms)
  are plain properties, used as `duration-(--duration-quick)`. `ease-standard` is
  `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`.

The generated `@theme` clears Tailwind's default `color`, `font`, `text`, `radius`, `shadow`,
`inset-shadow`, `drop-shadow`, `animate` and `ease` namespaces. Default classes such as
`bg-red-500`, `text-xl`, `shadow-lg` or `rounded-2xl` therefore compile to no CSS at all.

Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the duration tokens become `0ms`. Every element's animations
and transitions take 0.01ms, animations run once, smooth scrolling is off, and view transitions do
not animate. A looping indicator, such as a pending button's spinner, stops after one frame.

### Enforces the design system in lint

`eslint.config.js` applies these rules to `packages/ui/src/**` and, in advance of the app,
`apps/web/src/**`:

| Forbidden                                                                                      | Use instead                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A raw palette utility (`bg-red-500`, `hover:text-white`, `border-t-slate-200/50`, `bg-fog-10`) | A semantic utility (`bg-surface`, `text-ink-2`, `border-rule`)                                              |
| An arbitrary color (`bg-[#ff0000]`, `text-[oklch(…)]`)                                         | A semantic token; add one in `src/tokens/` if none fits                                                     |
| A color literal (`'#1a2b3c'`, `'oklch(0.5 0.1 200)'`, `rgb(`, `hsl(`)                          | A semantic utility. Short refs such as `'#07'` are not colors and stay legal                                |
| An inline style other than a custom property (`style={{ color: 'red' }}`, a spread)            | A utility, or a custom property read by a utility (`style={{ '--progress': '40%' }}` with `w-(--progress)`) |
| `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`                                                                      | Plain React rendering, which escapes text                                                                   |
| A `lucide-react` import (anywhere except `src/icons/registry.tsx`)                             | `<Icon name="…">` from the registry                                                                         |
| A Node built-in, `@yantra/core`, `@yantra/agent`, `@yantra/cli` or `@earendil-works/*`         | Nothing: the package is browser code                                                                        |
| A value import from `@yantra/protocol`                                                         | `import type` from `@yantra/protocol`                                                                       |

The token data directory (`packages/ui/src/tokens/`) is exempt from the color and inline-style
rules only. The repository's rule against site-specific names still applies throughout
`packages/ui/src`, including the token data and `.tsx` files.
`packages/ui/tests/boundary-rules.spec.ts` lints deliberately broken files under
`src/_lint-fixtures/` to prove that each rule fires, and that the clean fixture and the registry
stay clean.

### Serves every icon from one semantic registry

Components ask for an icon by meaning. `<Icon name="outcome.fulfilled" />` renders an SVG on
Lucide's 24 px grid, with a 1.75 stroke in `currentColor`, at 16 px (default) or 20 px.

- Without `label`, the icon is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`.
- With `label`, it is an image: `role="img"` and `aria-label`.
- Every icon carries `data-icon="<name>"`.

Names are `<category>.<camelCaseName>`:

| Category  | Names                                                                                            |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `outcome` | `fulfilled` (circle-check), `partial` (half-filled circle), `failed` (circle-x), `aborted` (ban) |
| `status`  | `needsYou` (hand), `info`                                                                        |
| `action`  | `stop`, `copy`, `close`, `openExternal`, `retry`                                                 |
| `nav`     | `chevronDown`, `chevronRight`, `check`                                                           |
| `field`   | `increment`, `decrement`                                                                         |
| `glyph`   | `bindu`, `contract`, `capture`, `handoff`, `protected`, `provenance`                             |

The six `glyph.*` names are Drshya's own drawings:

- `bindu`: a square inside a circle around a center point, for engine state;
- `contract`: a ring of requirement segments around a held center, for the task contract;
- `capture`: target brackets around a held frame;
- `handoff`: the run passing control across a boundary to the person;
- `protected`: a shield over hatching, for a protected value;
- `provenance`: the thread from goal to search to page to link.

Each glyph file in `src/icons/glyphs/` exports only its geometry. The registry wraps it with
Lucide's own `createLucideIcon`, so a glyph has exactly Lucide's SVG attributes. Drawing rules:
use only `circle`, `line`, `path` and `rect` elements; keep all geometry inside the 2 to 22 live
area of the 24 px grid; draw with strokes, never fills; and use no literal religious iconography.
The icon tests check the live area and the no-fill rule.

### Provides 16 accessible primitive families

Every primitive wraps a React Aria Components primitive, so keyboard, focus and screen-reader
behavior come from React Aria. Drshya adds the styling and its own rules. Keyboard focus shows a
2 px solid Ion (`accent`) outline, offset by 2 px, on every focusable element. Mouse focus shows no
ring. The ring passes 3:1 against `bg` and `surface` through the contrast gate.

| Family      | Exports                                                                             | Milestone |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| Button      | `Button`                                                                            | M1        |
| Link        | `Link`                                                                              | M1        |
| Tabs        | `Tabs`, `TabList`, `Tab`, `TabPanel`                                                | M1        |
| Tooltip     | `TooltipTrigger`, `Tooltip`                                                         | M1        |
| Disclosure  | `Disclosure`, `DisclosureTrigger`, `DisclosurePanel`                                | M1        |
| Toast       | `ToastProvider` (plus `createToastQueue`)                                           | M1        |
| Table       | `Table`                                                                             | M1        |
| TextField   | `TextField`                                                                         | M4        |
| NumberField | `NumberField`                                                                       | M4        |
| Checkbox    | `Checkbox`                                                                          | M4        |
| Switch      | `Switch`                                                                            | M4        |
| Popover     | `Popover`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverDialog`                                        | M4        |
| Select      | `Select`                                                                            | M4        |
| ComboBox    | `ComboBox`                                                                          | M4        |
| Dialog      | `Dialog`, `DialogTrigger` (also the AlertDialog variant)                            | M4        |
| Menu        | `Menu`, `MenuTrigger`, `MenuItem`, `MenuSection`, `MenuSeparator`, `SubmenuTrigger` | M4        |

The package root also exports the style recipes the primitives use (`buttonStyles`, `linkStyles`,
`tabStyles`, `fieldInputStyles`, `checkboxBoxStyles`, `switchTrackStyles`, `switchThumbStyles`,
`popoverStyles`, `optionStyles`), the `Option` list row, and the field building blocks described
below. `cn()` joins classes and resolves conflicts by Drshya's names: `cn('text-ink', 'text-ink-2')`
keeps only `text-ink-2`, while `cn('text-ink-2', 'text-body')` keeps both, because one is a color
and the other a size. `tv` is `tailwind-variants` bound to the same merger, and `focusRing` is the
shared ring recipe.

#### Button

Variants spend color on meaning, and there is no decorative color variant:

- `primary`: the one place to act, an `accent` fill with `on-accent` text;
- `secondary` (default): a plain control on `surface` with a `field-edge` border;
- `quiet`: `ink-2` text with no fill, for toolbars.

Sizes are `sm` and `md` (default). An optional `icon` takes a registry name. A button with no
children is icon-only, and its `aria-label` is required by type. If a cast gets around the type and
the label is empty, the button logs a console warning. `isPending` keeps the button focusable, blocks presses, and announces
progress with an indeterminate progress bar labeled "Pending". Disabled buttons use `ink-3` text on
`sunken`.

#### Link

`Link` treats every `href` as untrusted. `classifyHref(href)` parses it as a browser would and
returns one of three kinds:

| Kind       | Matches                                                                                           | Renders                                                                                                                            |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `internal` | Paths that stay in the app: `/runs/1`, `#summary`, `?q=1`                                         | A link in the same context                                                                                                         |
| `external` | An absolute `http:` or `https:` URL, or a protocol-relative one (`//host`)                        | A link with `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, the `action.openExternal` icon, and hidden "(opens in a new tab)" text |
| `unsafe`   | `javascript:` in any case, `data:`, `file:`, `blob:`, any other scheme, empty or unparsable input | Plain `ink-2` text, never an `<a>` element                                                                                         |

Link text uses `accent-ink` with an underline, so a link is never marked by color alone.

#### Tabs, Tooltip and Disclosure

- **Tabs**: arrow keys move between tabs (React Aria). The selected tab has an Ion underline and
  an extra-bold weight, so selection is not shown by color alone. The tab list uses `type-label`. A
  panel is focusable only when it has no focusable content.
- **Tooltip**: a solid inverse surface (`surface` text on `ink`), never glass. It opens after a
  600 ms hover (`TOOLTIP_DELAY_MS`), at once on keyboard focus, closes 200 ms after the pointer
  leaves (`TOOLTIP_CLOSE_DELAY_MS`), and closes on Escape. A tooltip adds to a name and never
  replaces one: the trigger keeps its own accessible name.
- **Disclosure**: the trigger is a quiet button with a chevron that turns when expanded. The turn
  uses `--duration-quick`, so reduced motion removes it. `DisclosureTrigger` takes an optional
  `headingLevel` (2 to 6) that wraps it in a heading. A collapsed panel is hidden from assistive
  technology. Controlled and uncontrolled use both work.

#### Toast

Toasts belong to the app, not to Drshya. `createToastQueue()` returns a queue instance, and
`<ToastProvider queue={queue}>` renders the region for it. There is no module-level queue, so two
providers with two queues never share toasts.

- `queue.add({ title, description?, tone, action? })` shows a toast and returns its key.
  `queue.close(key)` and `queue.clear()` remove toasts.
- **Tones** are `info`, `fulfilled`, `partial`, `failed` and `needs-you`. Each tone shows its
  registry icon in the graphic color and its word ("Info", "Fulfilled", "Partial", "Failed", "Needs
  you") in `ink-2`, so the tone is never color alone.
- **Timeout**: a toast without an `action` dismisses after 6 seconds (`TOAST_TIMEOUT_MS`). Hover
  and focus pause the timer. A toast with an `action` never dismisses on its own. Pressing the
  action runs `onAction` and closes the toast.
- **Announcements** are polite (`role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`), not assertive alerts.
- **Focus**: adding a toast never moves focus. Keyboard users reach the region with F6, React
  Aria's landmark navigation. Each toast has a labeled "Dismiss" button.
- Toasts are glass, stacked at the bottom-right corner of the viewport. At most 5 show at once
  (`maxVisibleToasts`), and the rest wait. `createToastQueue({ autoDismiss: false })` turns off the
  timeout for plain toasts, which the gallery uses for a stable screenshot.

#### Table

`Table` is a virtualized data table. It renders 10,000 rows with a bounded number of DOM rows,
because only the visible rows exist in the page.

- An accessible name is required by type, through `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- `columns` lists `{ id, header, cell(row), isRowHeader?, width?, align?, voice? }`. Exactly one
  column must set `isRowHeader`, or the table throws `TableContractError` on render in every build.
  That column names each row for screen readers.
- `voice: 'engine'` sets a column in `type-engine`, for IDs, URLs and refs.
- `rows`, `getRowKey(row)` and `emptyState` are required. `onRowAction(key)` is optional.
- `rowHeight` defaults to 40 px, and `height`, the scroll viewport, defaults to `24rem`. The header
  sticks to the top.

Paging is the caller's job. The table only asks for the next page:

| `loadState`           | What the table shows and does                                                                    |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `idle`                | Calls `onLoadMore` once when the end of the list scrolls into view                               |
| `loading`             | A "Loading more…" status row; never calls `onLoadMore`                                           |
| `error`               | A "Couldn't load more" row with a Retry button that calls `onLoadMore`; never retries on its own |
| `exhausted` (default) | Nothing more; never calls `onLoadMore`                                                           |

With no `onLoadMore`, the table never shows a load-more row. The caller keeps the cursor, appends
rows, and moves `loadState` back to `idle` when another page may exist.

#### Field anatomy and form controls

All form controls share one anatomy, so the label, description and error message are associated
with the input the same way everywhere:

- **Label**: `ink`, semibold. A required field shows the word "required", not only an asterisk.
- **Description**: `caption` size in `ink-2`.
- **Error**: shown only while the field is invalid, in `signal-failed-ink` with the
  `outcome.failed` icon.
- **Input**: a `sunken` surface with a `field-edge` border, which passes 3:1 on `bg`, `surface` and
  `sunken`, and `rounded-control` corners. An invalid input also gets a `signal-failed` border, so
  invalid state is never color alone.

`FieldLabel`, `FieldDescription`, `FieldErrorText` and `fieldInputStyles` are exported from the
package root, for building other fields. They are not one of the 16 families.

- **TextField**: single-line, or multi-line with `multiline`. `voice="engine"` sets the value in
  the mono voice.
- **NumberField**: locale formatting, `minValue`, `maxValue` and `step` come from React Aria.
  Labeled "Decrease" and "Increase" buttons step the value.
- **Checkbox**: when checked, an Ion fill with a check mark. When indeterminate, a dash, and
  `aria-checked="mixed"`.
- **Switch**: when on, an Ion track, the thumb at the end and a check mark in the thumb. The thumb
  moves at `--duration-quick`, so reduced motion removes the movement.

Checkbox and Switch focus a visually hidden native input. Their focus ring is drawn on the visible
box or track instead.

#### Overlays on glass: Popover, Select and ComboBox

`Popover` is the glass panel that Select, ComboBox and Menu share. React Aria handles placement and
flipping. Text inside it is only `ink` or `ink-2`. In Solid mode it turns opaque like any glass
surface.

- **Popover**: `PopoverTrigger` opens it, and `PopoverDialog` (with a required `aria-label`) holds
  freestanding content. Escape closes it, and focus returns to the trigger.
- **Select**: takes `options` (`{ id, label, isDisabled? }`). Enter, Space or Alt+Down opens the
  list, arrow keys move, and Enter selects, closes and returns focus to the trigger. The selected
  option shows a check mark. The placeholder (default "Select…") is `ink-2`.
- **ComboBox**: typing filters the options with a "contains" match. An empty result shows "No
  matches". Escape closes the list and keeps the typed text. `allowsCustomValue` passes through to
  React Aria.

A focused option shows the Ion outline. A selected option shows a check mark and a bolder weight.
Disabled options are `ink-2` and italic.

#### Dialog, AlertDialog and Menu

`Dialog` is modal. Its panel is a solid `surface`, never glass, with `rounded-frame` corners, over a
`--dialog-scrim` overlay (`bg` at 0.72 opacity). `title` is required and renders as the dialog's
heading. Children can be a function that receives `{ close }`.

- **Focus**: opening the dialog moves focus inside it. Tab stays inside the dialog. Closing it
  returns focus to the trigger.
- `role="dialog"` (default) closes on Escape or a click outside.
- `role="alertdialog"` is for confirmations. Escape and outside clicks do not close it, so the
  person must choose an explicit button.

`Menu` renders in the glass popover. It focuses its first item when it opens (`autoFocus`
defaults to `'first'`), and `placement` defaults to `'bottom start'`. Arrow keys and typeahead move
between items. Enter fires `onAction` and closes the menu. Disabled items are skipped.

- `MenuItem` takes a text label and an optional `icon`.
- `tone="destructive"` requires an `icon`, which is drawn in the `signal-failed` color. The label
  stays `ink`, as the glass text rule requires, and the item carries `data-tone="destructive"`.
  Meaning is never color alone.
- `MenuSection` groups items under a `title` header, and `MenuSeparator` draws a divider.
- `SubmenuTrigger` nests a menu, and its item shows a chevron.

### Runs under a strict CSP with no third-party requests

Drshya is built to run under the app's Content-Security-Policy, `default-src 'self'`:

- Fonts and the glass noise texture are files. The gallery's Vite build sets
  `assetsInlineLimit: 0`, because the policy blocks `data:` URIs.
- `drshya.css` contains no `http:` or `https:` URL and no `@import url(`. A unit test scans for
  them.
- React Aria normally adds an inline `<style id="react-aria-pressable-style">` at runtime, which the
  policy blocks. Drshya ships the same `touch-action` rule in `drshya.css`, and
  `prepareStrictCsp(document)` places a `<meta>` with that id, so React Aria skips the injection.
  It must run before the first render. A unit test checks the id against the installed React Aria
  source.
- Lint forbids `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, and `Link` never emits an unsafe URL.

The harness serves the gallery with exactly that policy and fails on any CSP violation or any
request to another origin.

### Proves every primitive in a gallery and a real-Chrome harness

The gallery is a React component exported from `@yantra/ui/gallery`, with its backdrop fixtures in
`@yantra/ui/gallery.css`. A standalone Vite page in `packages/ui/gallery/` serves it for development
and builds to `packages/ui/dist/gallery-site/` for the harness. The page reads its state from the
query string, `?entry=<id>&theme=light|dark|system&surfaces=glass|solid`. With no entry, or an
unknown one, it shows an index of entries.

It has 23 entries:

- five sheets: `tokens-colors`, `tokens-pairings`, `surfaces-glass` (a glass panel over black,
  white and a busy stripe pattern), `tokens-type-shape-motion` and `icons`;
- one entry per primitive family: `button`, `link`, `tabs`, `tooltip`, `disclosure`, `toast`,
  `table`, `text-field`, `number-field`, `checkbox`, `switch`, `popover`, `select`, `combo-box`,
  `dialog` and `menu`;
- `alert-dialog`, and `table-large` (10,000 rows).

`tests/gallery/completeness.spec.ts` fails if a barrel export belongs to no family, or if any of
the 16 families lacks exactly one gallery entry.

`e2e/drshya-gallery.spec.ts` (`@no-llm`) runs every entry in four states: light and dark, each in
Glass and Solid. It launches headless system Chrome at 1280×800 with an sRGB color profile, and
emulates reduced motion so frames are stable. For each state it checks that:

- the page loads with no CSP violation, page error or request to another origin;
- `axe-core` reports no violations;
- in interactive entries, every Tab stop shows an outline at least 2 px wide in the resolved Ion
  color;
- the screenshot matches the visual baseline.

Overlay entries (toast, popover, select, combo-box, dialog, alert-dialog, menu) render outside the
entry section, so their screenshot is the full page and axe and the focus walk cover the whole
document. In those runs, axe skips only its `region` rule, because landmark structure belongs to
the future app shell.

Further checks in the same suite:

- **Glass**: in both themes, the panel tint over black and white matches the composite model
  within 3/255 per channel. Glass mode has a backdrop filter. `data-surfaces="solid"`, and
  separately an emulated reduced-transparency setting, makes the panel opaque with no backdrop
  filter.
- **Type, shape and motion**: both font families load from the gallery's own origin. The engine
  voice uses Martian Mono at 87.5% width. A looping animation runs once under reduced motion.
  `rounded-2xl` has a 0 px radius, while `rounded-frame` is 14 px.
- **ComboBox**: in all four states, typing opens and filters the list, axe passes on the open list,
  and an unmatched query shows "No matches".
- **Large table**: at most 60 rows are in the DOM. Scrolling to the end requests one more page
  exactly once, and the last row is reachable.
- **System theme**: with no `data-theme`, the page follows a dark or light OS. `data-theme="light"`
  keeps light values under a dark OS.

## How to Use It

Run every command below from the repository root.

### Use Drshya in an app

No app consumes Drshya yet. A consumer imports `@yantra/ui/drshya.css` once, processes it with
Tailwind v4 (for example `@tailwindcss/vite`), and keeps Vite's `build.assetsInlineLimit` at `0`.
It then prepares the CSP and applies an appearance before the first render:

```tsx
import '@yantra/ui/drshya.css';

import {
  Button,
  ToastProvider,
  applyAppearance,
  createToastQueue,
  prepareStrictCsp,
} from '@yantra/ui';

prepareStrictCsp(document);
applyAppearance(document.documentElement, { theme: 'system', surfaces: 'glass' });

const toasts = createToastQueue();

export function App() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider queue={toasts}>
      <Button
        variant="primary"
        icon="action.retry"
        onPress={() => toasts.add({ tone: 'info', title: 'Run queued' })}
      >
        Run again
      </Button>
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}
```

A cursor-paged table, where the caller owns the cursor:

```tsx
<Table
  aria-label="Runs"
  columns={[
    { id: 'id', header: 'Run', cell: (run) => run.id, voice: 'engine', width: 140 },
    { id: 'goal', header: 'Goal', cell: (run) => run.goal, isRowHeader: true },
  ]}
  rows={runs}
  getRowKey={(run) => run.id}
  loadState={loadState}
  onLoadMore={loadNextPage}
  emptyState="No runs yet"
/>
```

A confirmation that only an explicit button can close:

```tsx
<DialogTrigger>
  <Button variant="secondary">Delete run</Button>
  <Dialog role="alertdialog" title="Delete this run?">
    {({ close }) => (
      <>
        <p>The run directory is removed.</p>
        <Button onPress={close}>Cancel</Button>
        <Button variant="primary" onPress={deleteRun}>
          Delete
        </Button>
      </>
    )}
  </Dialog>
</DialogTrigger>
```

### Change a token

1. Edit the data in `packages/ui/src/tokens/`: `palette.ts` for primitive values, `semantic.ts` to
   point a semantic name at another primitive, `pairings.ts` to declare a pairing, `glass.ts` for
   the glass recipe, or `scale.ts` for type, radius and motion.
2. Regenerate the CSS:

   ```bash
   pnpm --filter @yantra/ui emit:tokens
   ```

   If the data breaks the contract, the command exits 1 and prints every failure. Fix the values and
   run it again.

3. Check the result without writing it, as `build` does:

   ```bash
   pnpm --filter @yantra/ui emit:tokens --check
   ```

4. Run the unit tests, which include the contrast gate, the glass tests and the drift test:

   ```bash
   pnpm --filter @yantra/ui test
   ```

5. Commit the token change and `src/styles/theme.generated.css` together. A token change usually
   changes screenshots, so update the visual baselines too.

The glass tests pin the shipped tint (0.775 light, 0.8 dark). A change to the fog ramp or the glass
recipe that moves the floor must update those numbers on purpose.

### Add an icon

1. Add the name to `ICON_NAMES` in `packages/ui/src/icons/registry.tsx`, as
   `<category>.<camelCaseName>`. The `IconName` type follows from that list.
2. Add its record to `ICON_REGISTRY`. The `satisfies` clause makes a missing record a type error.
   - For a Lucide icon, import the component in `registry.tsx`, the only file that may import
     `lucide-react`, and register `lucide(Component)`. Check that the export exists in the pinned
     `lucide-react` 1.68.0. The registry test fails on a missing component.
   - For a custom glyph, add `src/icons/glyphs/<name>.ts` exporting a `GlyphNode`, and register
     `glyph('drshya-<name>', NODE)`. Follow the drawing rules above. The icon test pins the glyph
     list at six, so a new glyph updates that test too.
3. Run `pnpm --filter @yantra/ui test`. The `icons` gallery entry picks the new name up, so its
   visual baselines change.

### Add a primitive

Export the component from `packages/ui/src/primitives/index.ts`, add its family to
`PRIMITIVE_FAMILIES` in `src/primitives/families.ts`, and add one gallery entry in
`src/gallery/entries.tsx` with `primitive` set to the family and `interactive: true`. Set
`overlays: true` if React Aria portals part of it outside the entry. Helpers and style recipes go in
the package root (`src/index.ts`), not the primitives barrel, which may export only components.

### Open the gallery

Start the development page, then open the URL that Vite prints:

```bash
pnpm --filter @yantra/ui gallery
```

Add `?entry=button&theme=dark&surfaces=solid` to the URL to open one entry in one state.

### Run the tests and the harness

Unit tests and lint for the package:

```bash
pnpm --filter @yantra/ui test
pnpm --filter @yantra/ui lint
pnpm --filter @yantra/ui typecheck
```

The harness tests the built gallery and the built package, so build first. It needs a local Chrome
that core's `detectChrome` can find. A missing Chrome fails the suite with a remediation instead of
skipping it.

```bash
npx turbo run build
cd e2e && npx vitest run drshya-gallery.spec.ts drshya/
```

`drshya/` adds the server and visual-compare self-tests. The root `pnpm test` runs the harness too,
as part of the `e2e` workspace.

### Update visual baselines

Baselines are stored per platform, because font rendering differs between operating systems:

```text
e2e/drshya/baselines/<platform>/<entry>--<theme>--<surfaces>.png
```

`<platform>` is Node's `process.platform`: `linux`, `win32` or `darwin`.

- **Linux** is the required pixel gate, and CI runs it on `ubuntu-latest`. A missing or mismatched
  baseline fails.
- **Windows and macOS** compare only states that have a baseline on that platform. The others are
  skipped, and the test name gives the reason. The CSP, origin, axe and focus checks still run on
  every OS.
- A screenshot matches when at most 0.1% of its pixels differ, at a pixelmatch threshold of 0.1.

On a mismatch or a missing baseline, the harness writes `<name>.actual.png`, plus `<name>.diff.png`
when the sizes match, to `e2e/drshya/.out/`, which is gitignored. To write baselines for the
current platform instead of comparing:

```bash
cd e2e && UPDATE_DRSHYA_BASELINES=1 npx vitest run drshya-gallery.spec.ts
```

You can update Linux baselines from any machine. When the Linux CI job fails, the "Upload Drshya
gallery screenshots" step uploads `e2e/drshya/.out/` as the `drshya-gallery-<os>-<provider>`
artifact. Download it, review the `.actual.png` images, and commit the correct ones to
`e2e/drshya/baselines/linux/`, without the `.actual` suffix.

## Inputs and Outputs

Drshya has no runtime CLI input. Its inputs are:

- the token data in `packages/ui/src/tokens/*.ts`;
- component props, which are typed. The required names (Button icon-only `aria-label`, Table
  `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, Dialog `title`, PopoverDialog `aria-label`) are type errors
  when missing;
- untrusted strings: `Link` `href` (classified by `classifyHref`) and appearance strings (read by
  `parseAppearance`), which never pass through unchecked;
- the gallery query string: `entry`, `theme` and `surfaces`.

Its outputs:

| Output                                                         | Produced by                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `packages/ui/src/styles/theme.generated.css` (checked in)      | `pnpm --filter @yantra/ui emit:tokens`           |
| `packages/ui/dist/` (the package module and type declarations) | the package `build`                              |
| `packages/ui/dist/gallery-site/` (the standalone gallery)      | the package `build`                              |
| `e2e/drshya/.out/*.actual.png`, `*.diff.png`                   | the harness, on a missing or mismatched baseline |
| `e2e/drshya/baselines/<platform>/*.png`                        | the harness, with `UPDATE_DRSHYA_BASELINES=1`    |

Errors:

- `TokenContractError` lists every gamut, reference, contrast and glass-floor failure. Its
  `failures` property holds them as typed records. `emit:tokens` prints the message and exits 1.
- `TableContractError` is thrown on render when a table does not have exactly one row-header
  column.
- An icon-only `Button` with an empty accessible name logs a console warning.

Package exports: the root module `@yantra/ui`, the stylesheet `@yantra/ui/drshya.css`, the gallery
component `@yantra/ui/gallery`, and its fixtures `@yantra/ui/gallery.css`.

## Configuration and Permissions

Drshya reads no configuration file, preference, environment variable or secret, and writes nothing
under `~/.yantra`. Theme and surfaces are attributes set by the consumer through `applyAppearance`.

The harness reads one environment variable: `UPDATE_DRSHYA_BASELINES=1` writes baselines instead of
comparing them. It needs a discoverable local Chrome and binds its static server to `127.0.0.1` on
a free port. The gallery page may load resources only from that server: any other origin fails the
run. It needs no model provider or credentials.

## Limitations

- No Linux baselines are committed yet. The first Linux CI run fails the pixel step for every
  state and uploads the screenshots, and those images then become `e2e/drshya/baselines/linux/`.
  Until then, the pixel step cannot pass on Linux. No Windows or macOS baselines are committed
  either, so the pixel step is skipped on those platforms.
- No app mounts Drshya yet. `apps/web`, the in-app `/gallery` route, and the preferences that would
  feed `applyAppearance` belong to a later feature. The lint rules already cover `apps/web/src/**`.
- There is no compact density. Spacing is fixed at the 0.25rem base.
- React Aria 1.22.1 still names its toast API `UNSTABLE_*`. Drshya wraps those names inside
  `Toast.tsx`, so a React Aria upgrade may need changes there.
- The ComboBox gallery entry renders closed, because React Aria 1.22's ComboBox cannot be opened
  by a prop. Its open state is covered only by the harness test that types into it.
- React Aria has a second inline style injection, on iOS Safari's scroll-lock path only.
  `prepareStrictCsp` does not cover it.
- The harness checks accessibility with `axe-core` and the focus walk. It does not replace manual
  screen-reader passes, or 200% zoom and reflow checks on real app screens.
- Glass legibility is proven for `ink` and `ink-2` only. Any other text color on glass, including
  signal inks and `accent-ink`, is outside the guarantee and would need to pass the floor cap first.
